To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
binding of sialoglycopolymers to the human platelet surface totally immobilizes the membrane proteins and lipoids and increases the cytoplasm viscosity.
the carbohydrate binding to the cell surface totally restricts the membrane fluidity, which may be due to the cross linking of surface lectins.

binding of sialoglycoconjugates, such as sialic acid, mucin and fucose-containing glycosides, to the platelet membrane totally immobilizes the membrane proteins and liposomes, probably due to interaction with the surface lectins, and that this binding also results in an increase in cytoplasmic fluidity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the interaction of the carbohydrate with the cell membrane.
the role of carbohydrate recognition in cell adhesion and the effect of carbohydrate binding on the membrane fluidity.
elucidating the mechanism of the carbohydrate induced modulation of cell membranes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the binding of sialylated oligosaccharides to platelets induces a conformational change in the membrane proteins and lipopolysaccharides and also induces an increase in the viscosity of the cytoplasm.
binding of the carbohydrate ligand to the cell surface results in immobilization of the cell membrane, which in turn results in an increased viscosity of the cytoplasm.
the binding of carbohydrate to the cell surface results in immobilization of membrane proteins, lipids and cytoplasmic components.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the binding of these ligands results in the immobilization of the platelet membrane and the cytoplasm.
the carbohydrate ligands of P selectins and the E selectins induce cross-linking of surface lectins and also induce cross-linking between membrane components.
binding of sialoglycans and sulfated polysaccharides to the platelet surface results in immobilization of the membrane proteins and lipoproteins and increase in the cytoskeletal rigidity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the binding of these ligands to the platelet surface results in a dramatic immobilization of the membrane.
the carbohydrate induced immobilization of platelet surface membrane proteins and lipds is due to the interaction with P and E selectins.
binding of sialoglycoconjugate to the platelet membrane restricts the mobility and this is probably the mechanism of action of these compounds in inhibiting cell-cell adhesion and cell migration.
